item.title: Nicki Minaj Promises Fans Cash For Watch-Party Fashion Contest
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nicki Minaj promised fans cash for their "Million Dollar Pitch Competition" fashion posts and asked the Barbz to help pick winners.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj promised cash for fans’ fashion posts tied to her “Million Dollar Pitch Competition” watch party. The Barbz had their own prize contest as the show hit streaming.

The rapper named her first four winners on X on Tuesday night. She said more people had made the cut and asked fans to help choose the rest through polls.

“These are my first 4,” she wrote as she shared the first batch of entries. Her plan was to let the Barbz help decide who else would get a prize.

https://x.com/NICKIMINAJ/status/2112696275506475086

Her next posts split the field by style. One round focused on evening gowns, with three entries she labeled “Champagne glass,” “Pink carpet” and “Money chest.” She said that group would have just one winner.

She also put four more fans in a “PRETTY IN PANTS” group and told her followers she would post a poll for that round, too. Each post carried the #MillionDollarPitch and #MillionDollarFit tags.

https://x.com/NICKIMINAJ/status/2112698906803147080

https://x.com/NICKIMINAJ/status/2112699814425342098

The fan contest came as Minaj’s work as a judge reached viewers on Prime Video and YouTube. The Small Business Administration’s special paired her with Grant Cardone and Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia. Dean Cain served as host, and President Donald Trump also appeared. Minaj had discussed her judging role on Fox News in September.

The SBA contest’s $1 million prize pool came from Clover Network. Five small-business finalists competed for shares of the money, with $400,000 set aside for first place. Minaj’s posts about the Barbz promised “a few dollars” but did not name a cash amount for her fan prizes.

The contest was taped in Washington on September 18 before its October 20 streaming debut. Minaj kept the premiere going on X with both the fashion posts and a fresh show of support for Trump.

“Not going anywhere. Right where I need to be,” she wrote in response to a fan’s post about Trump calling her his favorite.

https://x.com/NICKIMINAJ/status/2112682756711030996

https://x.com/mayaminaj/status/2112679592930824214

Her stance followed her September appearance on “The Ingraham Angle” with SBA chief Kelly Loeffler to discuss the show. During that chat, Minaj said she would not make excuses for her support of the president.

For the fans picked in her first round, she closed with a promise and a joke: “You’ll be sent a few dollars. Don’t spend it all in one place.”

item.title: Anuel AA Barely Listens To Trap Now As Corridos Shape His Next Move
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Anuel AA opened up about his shift toward corridos and the family time behind his four-year wait to release a new album.
item.content:encoded:
Anuel AA said corridos had all but pushed trap and reggaeton out of his own playlist. Yet he still planned a return to the sounds that made him a star.

He shared plans for a full corridos album at Billboard Latin Music Week in Miami Beach. He said he had spent more of this year in Mexico than in the United States, EFE reported. He had also filled his time in the car with corridos. To him, their rise had brought a new style the music world needed.

He named Peso Pluma, Fuerza Regida, Tito Double P and Neton Vega among the acts he admired. They were friends, but he was also a fan of their work.

Part of the draw was how they sang. He praised their skill and the way many of them worked without Auto-Tune. He also felt the music shared some of trap’s street roots, though each style took its own approach. He called the full corridos set a gift for Mexico.

Yet his next move would still leave room for both sounds. His other planned album, “Real Hasta La Muerte 2,” would blend trap and reggaeton and build on his 2018 debut.

That interest had already led him to work with stars from the genre. In July, he joined Luis R Conriquez and Fuerza Regida on “Hay Con Que,” from Conriquez’s “Muchacho Alegre.” The official lyric video came out ahead of the album’s July 10 release.

He linked the four-year wait since “LLNM2” to a wish to live more fully. During the Billboard chat, he spoke about the time he wanted with his loved ones.

“I wanted to spend more time with my children and my family,” he said.

He had kept working while making room for that time. His most recent single, “Vuelve,” arrived on October 9.

He also shared “Los Veo,” a track from the corridos set made with producer Alex Torres. He linked that project to time spent in Mexico through some of his low points.

Anuel hoped to put both albums out together. He did not set a date, though he said he would celebrate the project on his November 26 birthday.

item.title: Funkmaster Flex Breaks Silence After All Hell Breaks Loose At Knicks Game
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Funkmaster Flex named Shadow Stokes after a Knicks game scuffle, denied taking a punch and promised more of his account Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Funkmaster Flex pushed back on claims that he was punched during a Knicks game scuffle, naming Shadow Stokes in two posts about the encounter.

The Hot 97 DJ posted a clip of the clash in a crowded hall. He then came back with a blunt response. “SHADOW STOKES COULD NEVER PUNCH ME!” he wrote.

The clip showed a group of men pressed together near a door. Arms stretched across the group, with hands on shoulders and backs. The camera then swung away from that group toward more people farther down the hall. Some stood and watched as the crowd moved past them.

The brief, partly blocked view did not show who started the clash. It also did not give AllHipHop a clear view of who struck whom. Flex, for his part, denied that he took a punch to the face.

View this post on Instagram

His first post paired a string of laughing emojis with questions about the clash. Flex asked when he had been assaulted and said he was minding his business. He then turned to someone he called Shadow and asked who had been with him. He did not name that other person.

In the next post, Flex used Stokes’ full name. He also placed his own words over the clip to push back on the punch claim. His message mocked that account of the clash rather than laying out how it began.

Stokes was not a new name in Flex’s world. The two had worked on the same record years before this clash. Credits for Flex’s 2005 “Carshow Tour CD & DVD” listed Stokes as a co-executive producer for Casino Entertainment. Flex was among the project’s executive producers. Koch Records put out the set more than two decades ago.

Stokes also worked on the label side. In a 2010 AllHipHop interview, DJ Kay Slay named him among E1’s radio staff as he discussed the team working his records. Flex did not say how his ties to Stokes reached this point.

The Knicks hosted the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday, October 20. Flex posted his latest response the next morning.

View this post on Instagram

He ended that post by promising more of his account Thursday at 7 p.m.: “I GOT A STORY TO TELL!”

item.title: LeBron James Gets Chippy, Cusses Out Heckling Knicks Fans At 76ers Debut
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: LeBron James got an earful from New York Knicks fans during his Philadelphia 76ers debut, but the NBA legend gave them a mouthful before he left Madison Square Garden. First of all, he walked away with a victory. Watch this though! The 41-year-old superstar and the Sixers opened his record 24th NBA season Tuesday night …
item.content:encoded:
LeBron James got an earful from New York Knicks fans during his Philadelphia 76ers debut, but the NBA legend gave them a mouthful before he left Madison Square Garden.

First of all, he walked away with a victory.

Watch this though!

The 41-year-old superstar and the Sixers opened his record 24th NBA season Tuesday night with a 106-100 win over the defending champion Knicks, whose fans apparently had some unfinished business with King James. He even has a special pin with “24” on it.

As LeBron approached the free throw line, the Garden erupted with a rather unwelcoming message.

“We don’t want you! We don’t want you!”

Now, that’s some New York hospitality!

James and his agent, Rich Paul, at one point indicated that New York would have been his preferred free agency destination if the Knicks hadn’t captured the chip. That was their first NBA championship since 1973, the year Hip-Hop was “born.” That is a long time!

Instead, LeBron landed in Philadelphia, where the Sixers have assembled a formidable collection of talent in pursuit of their first championship since 1983.

The Knicks might want to reconsider those chants. There was more, as seen above in the video.

James finished with 14 points and nine rebounds while Tyrese Maxey contributed 28 points. Jaylen Brown added 19, and Joel Embiid recorded 13 points and 11 rebounds. Great showing of force!

The Sixers also displayed some promising chemistry, which has not manifested fully yet. They had a nice 11-0 third quarter run.

“We did that on the fly,” James said…and with the Eagles not flying, Philly kinda needs this energy from the Sixers.

Y’all know it’s wild when Spike Lee attempts to calm a situation. Imagine Spike Lee negotiating a Knicks ceasefire during opening night!? Wild night!

Big Bron did nothing to diminish the significance of New York’s championship celebration.

“I wouldn’t say that,” James said. “It was a great night for New York fans. Fifty-plus years. I was a part of that at one point where we hadn’t won a major championship in Cleveland in over 50 years. The fans will never forget this moment.”

The biggest question is whether James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey can translate their impressive individual résumés into a championship. That is truly all that matters and they have two years to accomplish it.

For now, LeBron has one victory, Knicks fans have their banner, and the Eastern Conference has a fascinating new rivalry.

We gon’ see!

item.title: Mistah F.A.B. Gets E-40’s Name In WNBA Finals TV Mix-Up
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Mistah F.A.B. sat beside Too $hort at the WNBA Finals, but a USA Sports graphic identified the Oakland rapper as E-40.
item.content:encoded:
Mistah F.A.B. had a front-row seat at the WNBA Finals next to Too $hort. The name on TV did not match his face.

A shot from Monday night’s Game 2 showed a graphic that called him E-40. The words “E-40” and “RAPPER” sat beside him on the USA Sports feed.

The two Bay Area stars were at Chase Center as the Golden State Valkyries faced the Atlanta Dream. In the shot, Too $hort wore a Valkyries jersey on the left. F.A.B. wore a hat and glasses on the right.

A viewer posted the shot on X late on Monday, October 19, and called out the wrong name. The image was a photograph of a television screen. SFGATE also named Mistah F.A.B. in its own courtside photo from the game.

https://x.com/ERRICAMACK/status/2112364657205715207

The name on screen was not the only link to Bay Area rap that night. Too $hort had been booked to lead the pregame drum. LaRussell was set for halftime. AllHipHop had laid out those plans before the game.

The courtside seats also put two old friends side by side. F.A.B. had known $hort since he was a child.

In a 2022 AllHipHop interview, F.A.B. explained what Too $hort meant to him.

“Short took me to Atlanta a long time ago, showed me how to move around. I call Too Short pops. He’s a godfather-like figure in my life. I’ve been knowing him since a kid, personally knowing him since 9 or 10 years old.”

He said $hort was both an idol and a friend. He could go to him for help with his music and his life.

He also praised $hort as a Hip-Hop great.

“He’s so humble, but he’s a legend. That’s a legend.”

That bond also made it onto a Snoop Dogg song. F.A.B. and $hort joined him on “Life Of Da Party.” F.A.B. recalled how they ran into Snoop at a Hollywood building and went on to make the track.

On the court, Atlanta won 79-65 to tie the best-of-seven series at one game each. Angel Reese led the Dream with 30 points and 16 rebounds, while Rhyne Howard set a Finals record with six steals. Atlanta scored 24 points off Golden State’s 19 turnovers.

Game 3 is set for October 21 at 8 P.M. Eastern at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. The split also ensured a return to Chase Center for Game 5 on October 26.

item.title: Lil Baby Calls On Future & Young Thug For “FRESH”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Baby lined up Future, Young Thug and Rylo Rodriguez for "FRESH," his 17-track album set to arrive on November 6.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Baby named Future and Young Thug as guests on the same track for “FRESH.” His next album is due November 6, with a full song list now out ahead of the release.

The two Atlanta stars will join him and Rylo Rodriguez on “All My Partnas,” one of 17 songs on the digital tracklist his team shared. Rylo also has a spot on “In Your Head.” Those are the only two songs with named guests on the list, leaving Lil Baby to carry most of the album himself.

The album follows “WHAM” and “The Leaks,” the two full-length projects Lil Baby put out last year. His team confirmed the date and song list in a new announcement, with preorders now open through his official store.

Lil Baby, Future and Young Thug have a hit behind them as a trio. The three teamed up on “Dum, Dumb, And Dumber,” a track from “WHAM” that entered the Hot 100 at No. 16 in January 2025.

That song was part of the launch of “WHAM,” which went straight to the top of the Billboard album chart.

Rylo’s two guest spots also keep Lil Baby’s own label in the mix. He was the first artist signed through Glass Window Entertainment’s deal with Motown and Capitol in 2023. Lil Baby founded the label. The two had already worked together on Rylo’s “Been One” album when that deal was announced.

“Dead Fresh” also made the cut for the new album. Pharrell Williams produced the song, which Lil Baby first played at Louis Vuitton’s men’s show in Paris in June. The track came out in July, months before the full project was due.

It was Lil Baby’s first song with Pharrell, his label said when the video came out. Kid Art directed that clip, which carried the song’s fashion theme from tennis and golf looks to a front-row seat at a runway show.

His team also opened orders for signed vinyl and CDs alongside the album news.

Fans in Atlanta will have a show on the calendar soon after. Lil Baby had already announced his “Fresh Prince Of Atlanta” birthday concert at State Farm Arena for December 5, less than a month after “FRESH” is due.

item.title: The Tragic Coincidence Connecting Lil Durk And NBA YoungBoy
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Two viral lookalikes of Lil Durk and NBA YoungBoy reportedly met tragic ends.
item.content:encoded:
This is something that came to my attention recently. Lil Durk has an odd link to a young man who became an internet sensation off his likeness. This was simply because he looked remarkably like the Chicago rapper. There is a sad side to that. And there is another kid that looks like NBA YoungBoy and he met the same fate.

This is one of those stories that makes you wonder about the strange relationship between internet celebrity and real life.

According to reports circulating online, Deanta, better known as “Baby Durk,” was fatally shot in 2026. He was reportedly just 20 years old. That is so young.

Baby Durk developed an online following because of his resemblance to Lil Durk. With looking like a celebrity can generate an audience almost overnight, the young man became recognizable without necessarily having the musical accomplishments of the person he resembled.

But there is another chapter to this story and his as tragic.

Way back in January 2022, “NCAA YoungBoy” reportedly suffered a similarly violent fate. His nickname was Lil Pnut. He gained attention because of his resemblance to NBA YoungBoy. According to accounts of the incident, Lil Pnut was found fatally shot in Union Springs, Alabama. He was reportedly 21 years old. It is best not to do cosplay as alleged gang related rappers.

Now, four years later, the reported death of Baby Durk has people revisiting that earlier tragedy.

The similarities are unsettling to say the last. Viral lookalikes that died violently. WTF.

We do not know the nature of their deaths or if their lookalike status had something to do with it.

The internet can turn ordinary people into mini-celebrities without giving them the protection or even respect.

For now, not about celebrity resemblance and mostly about two young lives that ended far too soon.

Rest in peace to both young men. Sorry we’re bringing it to y’all this way.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Diddy May Represent Himself As Lawyers Exit Civil Case
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Diddy faced the prospect of handling his $100 million suit alone as his lawyers sought to quit over disputed bills and lack of contact.
item.content:encoded:
Diddy may end up representing himself in his $100 million lawsuit now that his lawyers want to drop him over what they called his refusal to pay.

Sher Tremonte said Diddy had paid it nothing for more than seven months in an October 15 filing in Thalia Graves’ suit. They also said they could not get him to discuss his cases, leaving the firm unable to do its job.

That split could leave Diddy without a lawyer in the suit he brought against Courtney Burgess, Ariel Mitchell and Nexstar, which owns NewsNation. He first sought $50 million over claims he said were false. He later raised that sum to $100 million. But before that fight can move on, Judge John P. Cronan needs to know who will handle his case.

Diddy had pushed back on the bills. Through spokesman Juda Engelmayer, Diddy told USA TODAY he chose to switch firms over bills he had not approved. He also said lawyer Jonathan Davis would take over the NewsNation suit at the right time.

That was in September. Yet the firm’s October 19 letter named no new lawyer for this case. A person on Diddy’s team said he had begun “exploratory” talks about new counsel for him or his firms. The talks could cover other cases as well, so the firm still had no clear plan for this suit.

“[N]either Mr. Combs, nor his power of attorney, nor any other authorized representative has identified replacement counsel in this matter or confirmed whether or not Mr. Combs intends to proceed pro se,” the firm wrote.

Diddy had not told the court he planned to represent himself, and the firm’s request to withdraw still awaited a ruling.

His lawyers had tried for weeks to learn what he would do. They sent the court’s order to the person with power of attorney for Diddy in September. Two more emails this month drew no reply, they said.

“On October 14, we also mailed the Court’s Order to Mr. Combs and included in that mailing a request that he advise whether he had engaged new counsel,” the lawyers wrote.

They then learned he had moved from Fort Dix to Allenwood. On October 16, they sent the same papers to his new prison.

The firm won its bid in Shante Kelly’s suit against Diddy. Judge Valerie Caproni let it leave on October 13. She found good cause to let the firm go: it had not been paid, and its work with Diddy had broken down. Her ruling also let the firm hold his files until it was paid. To set that sum, the judge still needed proof of how much he owed.

The firm used that ruling to back its bid to leave the Burgess suit. Its fight over fees had spread across Diddy’s cases. But the order in Kelly’s suit did not let it walk away from all of them.

The split has slowed work on the suit. Judge Cronan paused the sharing of evidence while the firm sought to leave. He said he would set a new status conference if a new lawyer appeared for Diddy.

item.title: Spotify’s AI Remix Push Gives Indie Artists Two Chances To Say No
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Spotify's Believe deal would let indie acts opt into paid AI remixes, while leaving artists a separate choice on whether to join.
item.content:encoded:
Spotify signed a deal with Believe that would let fans make AI covers and remixes of songs by artists who choose to take part. For indie acts, saying yes to AI talks would not mean accepting this tool.

The October 20 deal covered artists and labels served by Believe and TuneCore. Artists would first opt in to hear about AI plans, the firms said. They could then accept or turn down Spotify’s offer on its own.

The planned tool would cost extra on top of Spotify Premium. It would let fans rework songs, not make wholly new works. Streams would pay royalties to the artists and rights holders behind the source music, and each remix would link back to the original song and artist.

The firms could sign a deal, but the artists would still have their own choice. The news release did not name any rappers or singers who had signed up. It also did not spell out their share of the money.

Spotify had already struck deals for the tool with Universal Music Group in May, Merlin in August and Kobalt that same month. Music Business Worldwide reported that the service still had not announced a price or launch date.

The deal came as Hip-Hop’s debate over AI reached past who gets paid. In a recent AllHipHop interview, Young Guru drew a line between tools that help people work and tools that do the creative work for them.

“I can’t stand the creative AI. There’s no reason for it,” the longtime JAY-Z engineer said.

Young Guru said he did not use it to create, though he did not reject AI that helps with tasks. He also raised concerns about who controls those tools and what they can learn about people’s private lives. Those remarks came before the new deal, not as a response to it.

Spotify also released new figures on its efforts to keep spam out of fans’ feeds. It said it had kept more than 50 million tracks it classed as spam or low-value content out of song suggestions this year. That was separate from more than 75 million tracks removed from the service for serious or repeated rule breaches.

Its profile-protection tool, which lets artists review releases that use their names, remained in a test phase. Spotify said it planned to open that tool to all artists by the end of the year.

item.title: 702 Learns To Sing Through Grief After Irish Grinstead’s Death
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 702's LeMisha Fields and Meelah Williams opened up about performing without Irish Grinstead and finding new meaning in old hits.
item.content:encoded:
702‘s LeMisha Fields and Meelah Williams are learning to sing through the loss of Irish Grinstead. As their first album turns 30, its songs mean more to them than they did as teens.

Fields told Las Vegas Weekly that she chose to keep singing to honor her late sister, rather than stay locked in grief.

“She would want us to continue and live out the legacy of 702. It’s a bittersweet kind of thing,” Fields said.

Irish died at 43 in September 2023. Fields lost both a sister and a voice she knew from the stage. The pair had grown up together, then built their careers in the same group. Their family had also lost Irish’s twin, Orish. A founding member of 702, she died in April 2008 at 27.

Both Fields and Williams are now moms. Williams said love, loss and heartbreak had changed what “Get It Together” meant to her. It was no longer just the sad breakup song she knew as a girl. Back then, they split their time between school and the studio.

“Get It Together” came out on “No Doubt,” the group’s first album. Motown and Biv 10 Records released it on October 8, 1996. The song reached No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100. A tale of love in trouble had taken the group far beyond its Las Vegas home.

Missy Elliott joined them on “Steelo.” Donell Jones and The Characters also helped make the album, which went gold. It holds the songs they are singing now. Both hits date to that first album, before the later losses that changed the group.

The music has found new life through Summer Walker, too. She sampled “Get It Together” on “Body,” from her 2019 debut “Over It.” When her label shared the video in January 2021, it pointed to that link with 702. The sample brought the group’s work into a new R&B star’s song.

Williams said young fans told them they heard 702 through their parents.

The duo will mark 30 years at On the Record at Park MGM on October 23. A skate night at Skate Rock City follows October 24.
